title: Analyze Analytics data with an LLM or MCP
lead: Use an aggregate file, Observability Assistant or MCP for analysis. Define the query conditions and authorized sharing or access scope first.

blocks.text: Choose how the assistant receives data

rows: Prepare the required JSON or CSV through your API/export workflow and supply it to an approved LLM. It analyzes the file without connecting to Analytics.
Ask in the external Dashboard chat, which retrieves data within your account permissions. Use Download Chat before leaving if you need a record.
Connect a compatible AI client to the official server. Review the dataset and query scope before requesting data.

blocks.text: These tools run outside Player Lab. The app has no LLM chat, MCP connection form or account-data export button.

items: Define the question and period; for example, compare startup by browser over two completed days in UTC.
Retain start/end, time zone, metric, aggregation, units, filters, groupings, interval, ordering and limit with the result. Use a non-confidential dataset label rather than a license key.
Include each group’s population under the same conditions. Distinguish missing or suppressed data from zero; do not derive a period median from hourly medians.

Remove credentials, viewer/session IDs, IP addresses, source URLs and unreviewed custom fields. Aggregate or suppress small groups under your sharing rules. A raw CSV is not automatically safe to upload.
Review the file locally and send only necessary fields to an approved AI service. Keep the original query and output under your control.

blocks.text: Replace the scope below with your aggregate file’s conditions. This is an unexecuted prompt template, not a finding about Player Lab usage. Both editions include the same English template.

blocks.title: Aggregate-file prompt template
blocks.text:
Analyze only the attached, reviewed aggregate dataset. Do not request credentials or session-level records.

Question: Did video startup time change by browser between the two supplied UTC days?
Scope: Dataset A; 2026-10-18T00:00:00Z through 2026-10-20T00:00:00Z.
Metric: median VIDEO_STARTUPTIME, milliseconds, filter VIDEO_STARTUPTIME > 0.
Population: eligible video starts from a separate count query with the same time range and filters.

1. Check the metadata, units, group sizes, missing buckets and any row limit before comparing results.
2. Compare only the supplied days and groups. Do not average medians or treat missing/suppressed values as zero.
3. Return a table with values, absolute changes, relevant counts and caveats. State any unit conversion.
4. Separate measured observations from hypotheses. A browser correlation does not establish the cause.
5. Propose the smallest follow-up queries, with exact metric/aggregation/filter/time requirements, without executing them.
6. Include the dataset scope and query conditions in the answer so the comparison can be repeated.
Connect the official Observability MCP server

MCP (Model Context Protocol) lets AI clients call server tools. The official endpoint, https://analytics.mcp.bitmovin.com/, uses x-api-key authentication and optional x-tenant-org-id tenant selection. Follow the current official steps for your client; the Claude Desktop example uses Node.js 20 or later.

The configuration uses placeholders. Store real credentials only in protected local MCP settings through the client’s secret mechanism. Keep them out of prompts, Player Lab fields, committed files, screenshots and shared conversations. MCP grants a data-access path separate from sharing an aggregate file.
Ask for the right tool and scope

rows: Use the connected catalog. searchMetrics and searchFilters provide focused lookup when available; getAvailableMetrics and getAvailableFilters return full lists.
queryTotal: aggregates such as totals, averages, medians and percentiles.
query: time series and chart with automatically selected buckets.
queryGroupBy: category breakdowns. Keep the period and filters consistent.
getImpressionOverview summarizes one impressionId; analyzeImpression adds a timeline and interpretation. Neither replaces license-wide totals or period queries.

blocks.text: Tool keywords may differ from Dashboard labels or REST fields. Resolve them in the catalog and retain definitions, aggregation and units. Keep Error Percentage distinct from Error Ratio, and avoid conditions that change a calculated rate’s denominator.

items: Specify the authorized dataset, start/end and time zone. Ask to see the resolved metric, aggregation and filters before querying.
Use queryTotal for the whole period and query for a trend. Record the time-series buckets, which are chosen automatically.
Use queryGroupBy for browser or device differences. Request corresponding population counts separately when needed.
Only when aggregate evidence calls for it, explicitly authorize a narrowly scoped single-session investigation. Session IDs identify sessions rather than count viewers.
Retain tool inputs, results and explanation. Check calculations and proposed follow-ups against the results before changing playback settings.

blocks.text: The MCP documentation distinguishes thresholds on individual timings from cumulative session-time conditions, which those filters do not support. Session tools accept one impressionId rather than a period. A fluent answer does not establish that an unsupported query ran.

items.label: Check metric names, units and populations
